turns.user: Inverse-design a printable mortar: 28-day compressive strength >= 40 MPa and static yield stress between 1 and 4 kPa, minimising the clinker fraction. Search space: OPC required 0.5-1.0, silica fume 0-0.15, limestone powder 0-0.3, w/b 0.28-0.45. Run without asking.
turns.text:
I’ll run the inverse design immediately using the specified bounds, treating the mix as 3D-printable mortar and applying the stated 28-day targets. I’ll report all optimizer defaults and model limitations returned by the tool.
The first search found low-clinker candidates, but its probabilistic acceptance rule allowed median yield stress just below 1 kPa because uncertainty overlaps the target. I’m tightening the yield-stress satisfaction threshold once so the recommendation better reflects the requested interval.
No fully robust solution was found within the search space. The best provisional low-clinker candidate is:

- Binder: OPC 70%, limestone powder 30%, silica fume 0%
- w/b: 0.285
- s/b: 2.07
- Clinker fraction: 0.70
- 28-day compressive strength: 46.10 [27.20, 77.65] MPa
- Static yield stress at discharge: 0.941 [0.017, 4.628] kPa
- Target probabilities: strength 0.66; yield-stress range 0.35
- Joint feasibility probability: 0.23

Thus, the median strength exceeds 40 MPa, but the median yield stress is slightly below 1 kPa and its uncertainty is very large. Tightening the yield-stress acceptance probability to 0.50 produced zero feasible candidates; the optimizer had to relax the thresholds.

The minimum feasible clinker fraction identified was 0.70, despite the theoretical lower bound of 0.55. No training-range violation was reported.

Assumptions/defaults: 3DCP mortar, moist curing, 50-mm compression cube, static yield stress at 0 s rest, and no admixtures. The optimizer sampled s/b because none was specified.

This is only a material-property screen—not a physical printability verdict. Geometry, layer cycle time, open time, buckling, and plastic collapse were not assessed. Experimental rheology and strength verification are essential.
